summary: Emma Georgina Rothschild is a historian who studied at Somerville College, Oxford, and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. She served as a professor at the University of Cambridge (~1991–2008) and held a post at Harvard University (~2008).

Emmanuel Levinas (1906–1995) worked in philosophy and religious studies. After studying at Strasbourg and Freiburg, where he studied under Martin Heidegger, he held posts at the University of Poitiers (~1961–1967), University of Paris (~1973–1976), and University of Fribourg (~1976–1980).

Emmie te Nijenhuis is an Indologist who completed her PhD under Jan Gonda at Utrecht University, also studying at Utrecht Conservatory and Utrecht School of the Arts. She taught Indian musicology at Utrecht University (1964–1988) and held a post at the University of Amsterdam.

Enamul Haque (1937–2022) was an archaeology and Indology scholar educated at the University of Dhaka and Oxford. He served as Director General of the Bangladesh National Museum (1983–1991) and headed the International Centre for Study of Bengal Art (~1995–2022).

Encho Tamura (1917–2013) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and Japanology. Educated at Kyushu and Kyoto universities, he was a professor at Kyushu University (1968–1980) and Kumamoto University (-1982), and directed the Kyushu Historical Museum (~1982–1992).

Endo Asai (1927–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University. He served as a professor at Rissho University from 1972 (emeritus 1997) and as president of Minobusan University (1998–2001).

Eng Jin Ooi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD in Buddhist Textual Studies at Mahidol University (attested 2021), supervised by Giuliano Giustarini, Peter Skilling, and Kengo Harimoto.

Enga Teramoto (1872–1940) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Kumbum Monastery in 1903. He served as a professor at Otani University (1915) and as a lecturer at Kyoto University (~1921–1930).

Enichi Ocho (1906–1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Daijō Tokiwa. He worked as a researcher at the Academy of Oriental Culture (1931) and became professor emeritus at Otani University (1949–1976).

Enryo Inoue (1858–1919) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Ernest Fenollosa and Tanzan Hara. He founded Toyo University in 1887, where he served as lecturer and manager (~1887–1905).

Ensho Kanakura (1896–1987) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Tohoku University (1923–1929) and Rissho University (~1959–1978), and served as president of Miyagi University of Education (1967).
Ensho Nasu is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD under Esho Mikogami at Ryukoku University (attested 1996), where he later served as a visiting researcher (attested 2007).

Enshu Kurumiya is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD under Jan Willem de Jong at the Australian National University in 1974 and served as a professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University (attested 1981–1985).

Entai Tomomatsu (1895–1973) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Keio University (~1917–1923), founded the Publishing Association of Abhidharmakosa-vyakhya, and held a post at Taisho University.

Erberto Lo Bue (1946–2022) was a Tibetologist and historian who earned his PhD from SOAS University of London (~1976–1981). He lectured in Tibetan language and literature at the University of Milan (~1994–2002) and held a post at the University of Bologna (~2002–2016).

Eric David Mortensen is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2003) under the doctoral supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp, Michael Witzel, and Kimberley C. Patton.

Eric Grinstead (1921–2008) worked in sinology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies after studying at Victoria University of Wellington. He held posts at the British Library (~1957–1970) and the Nordic Institute of Asian Studies (1969).
Eric Huntington is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under the doctoral supervision of Gary A. Tubb.

Eric J. Sharpe (1933–2000) was a religious studies scholar and Indologist. Educated at Manchester and Uppsala universities, he held the First Chair of Religious Studies at the University of Sydney (1977–1996) and a professorship at Uppsala University (1978–1981).

Eric M. Greene is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD from the University of California, Berkeley (2012) under Robert H. Sharf and became an assistant professor of religious studies at Yale University (attested 2017).
